summary: Dune is a tense multiplayer negotiation game where public alliances and private side-deals matter as much as the area-control battles fought over Arrakis' spice and strongholds. Combat is resolved through simultaneous secret bidding of force strength and traitor cards, so most games turn on bluffing, betrayal, and timing rather than raw military strength.
praised: Negotiation and diplomacy phase is the heart of the game and creates memorable table dynamics
Asymmetric factions with genuinely different win conditions and abilities keep replays fresh
Traitor cards and secret alliances create high-tension bluffing moments
Faithful, thematic recreation of the novel's factions and politics
criticised: Long playtime and heavy downtime when not directly involved in a negotiation
Steep rules overhead and asymmetric faction powers make teaching difficult
Kingmaking and runaway-leader dynamics can frustrate players late game
Needs a full table of engaged players; weaker with fewer than 5-6 or with quiet/non-negotiating groups

interaction.kind: negotiation, alliance-forming, bluffing, and open conflict

scoring.why: the game ends the instant a faction meets its specific victory condition (usually controlling enough strongholds, or a faction-specific alternate win), so there is no cumulative scoring at all

similar: Rex: Final Days of an Empire
